sources.summary: Washington Blade (10 Apr 2025): trans activists in Buenos Aires say President Milei's policies have made the community's situation chaotic and desperate, more vulnerable to violence, discrimination and poverty; his government closed the Women, Gender and Diversity Ministry and INADI (2024) and dismissed trans public-sector workers hired under the Trans Labor Quota Law; the country's former special envoy for LGBTQ rights says LGBTQ+ people are in a bad moment for rights and quality of life. National picture, April 2025.

Agencia Presentes (19 Mar 2026): the National Hate-Crime Observatory counts a record 2025 — at least 227 crimes based on sexual orientation or gender identity, up 62% year-on-year, one every 38 hours; most perpetrators were security-forces personnel or strangers in public spaces, with beatings the leading modality; security-force violence cases rose from 17 (2024) to 64 (2025). Named provincial incidents: police interventions in the deaths of three LGBT+ people in Salta, Córdoba and Buenos Aires provinces (18–26 Nov 2025), and a provincial prison-service raid in Buenos Aires province (14 Apr 2025).

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 500); the underlying source covers decree 62/2025 amending the Gender Identity Law (banning transition treatments for under-18s) and a companion decree on the housing of trans people in prisons — both challenged in court as unlawful. National-level: applies to every unit.
